sub_industry: Integrated Delivery Network & Medicare Advantage Health Plan
operating_regions: 34-hospital regional footprint across Illinois, Indiana and Wisconsin; Meridian Medical Group affiliated practices across the same multi-state service area
business_model: Vertically integrated delivery system (34 owned hospitals, 214 ambulatory clinic sites, employed and affiliated physician network) paired with an owned health plan. Revenue splits 60% provider / 40% health plan; plan revenue splits 70% Medicare Advantage and Medicare FFS / 30% commercial and Medicaid managed care.
customer_segments: Medicare Advantage members; Medicare fee-for-service beneficiaries; commercial health plan members; Medicaid managed-care members; self-pay and commercially insured patients across acute, ambulatory and behavioral health service lines
mission: Deliver connected, measurably better health outcomes for the communities Meridian serves by unifying clinical care and health plan operations under one accountable system.
vision: Be the region's most trusted integrated health system, closing care gaps proactively through data rather than reactively through claims review.
strategic_priorities: 1) Improve Medicare Advantage overall Star Rating from 3.5 to 4.5+ stars by measurement year 2028; 2) Begin modernizing the on-premises SQL Server datamart sprawl by evaluating Databricks as a future lakehouse target — evaluation-stage only, nothing implemented yet; 3) Expand Epic Community Connect to affiliated practices to reduce interface sprawl; 4) Reduce claims denial write-offs and RAF evidence gaps; 5) Govern AI use cases with human-in-the-loop review as they move from concept to pilot
leadership_team: President & CEO; COO; CFO; CIO; CMIO; CNO; CMO; CDAO; CISO; CHRO; CLO; CQO; President, Meridian Health Plan; President, Meridian Medical Group
current_state_notes: Epic (Hyperspace/Chronicles/Clarity/Caboodle and 25+ additional modules) anchors clinical and revenue-cycle operations across the 34 owned hospitals and Meridian Medical Group's employed clinics. The data and analytics estate is entirely on-premises today: dozens of discrete SQL Server datamarts (one per domain — finance, quality/STARS, risk adjustment, revenue cycle, clinical operations, and more), fed primarily by Epic Clarity extracts, with Tableau Server as the dominant on-prem self-service BI layer on top. There is no live production cloud data or analytics platform of any kind. One acquired hospital (St. Anselm Community Hospital) still runs a legacy Cerner instance pending Epic conversion.
target_state_notes: Leadership has just begun evaluating Databricks as a future lakehouse target to rationalize the SQL Server sprawl — this is a planning-stage initiative with a vendor demo and a one-page brief on file, no signed contract, no pilot workload, and no migrated data. Tower and Source workstreams should treat 'all on-prem today, cloud lakehouse under evaluation' as the current-state fact, not smooth it into a cloud-native narrative that doesn't exist yet.
